title: Volatile Products at Thermal Loading of Spruce Wood
content: During the burning of wood, various toxic compounds are produced; therefore, fire retardants are used. However, fire retardants also produce toxic compounds, so the effort is to find low-cost, efficient, and environmentally friendly alternatives. We combined a highly durable polyurea (P) coating with expandable graphite (EG), which is very effective against fire. We thermally loaded untreated spruce wood and specimens treated with different coating combinations using an infrared heater. Volatile compounds were analysed by gas chromatography coupled with mass spectrometry (GC-MS) and high-performance liquid chromatography (HPLC). Various groups of volatile substances were determined, including terpenes (alpha- and beta-pinene, limonene), acids (formic, acetic), carbonyl compounds (formaldehyde, acetaldehyde, furfural, 5-hydroxymethylfurfural), and sulfur trioxide. The addition of EG to polyurea significantly increases the resistance of spruce wood to thermal loading while simultaneously reducing the amount of arisen volatile gases. An optimal combination of EG and P was identified to ensure effective thermal resistance and low concentrations of evolved gases.
